mappings.note: Identifying a pesticide anchors on the only outcome that mentions pesticides, the controlled-use one. Duplicate of an earlier item in this chapter and coded the same way; not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which covers field operations rather than agrochemicals.
The seed drill as a sowing implement is a crop-production practice. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, which needs a model built and explained.
When rabi crops are harvested is the kharif/rabi classification named verbatim in the outcome. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1: the pupil sorts by season rather than performing a practice.
Placing maize in the rainy season is the same seasonal classification applied to a named crop. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, since no cause is being traced.
The implement for weed removal is a production practice. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, because mechanical weeding involves no agrochemical to restrain.
Transplanting seedlings is a sowing practice that raises yield. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, since no crop is being classified.
Compost as natural manure is the organic counterweight to chemical fertiliser, where the frame locates input judgement. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which fits the field operation rather than the input.
BHC as an insecticide sits on the controlled-use-of-pesticides outcome. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, whose classification examples cover organisms and materials like metals, not agrochemicals.
Defining fertilisers as nutrient-rich chemicals belongs with the fertiliser judgement outcome. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no effect is being traced to a cause.
Threshing, separating grain from chaff, is a post-harvest production step. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, since no investigation is conducted.
Humus from decayed organic matter is the natural soil resource that sits beside manure in the judicious-use outcome. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which covers operations rather than the soil's own material.
Irrigation as the timed supply of water is a production practice. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, because no conservation judgement is asked for.
The khurpi for hand weeding is a production operation. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, as no chemical is involved.
The sprayer is defined by the weedicide it applies, placing it on the controlled-use outcome. Deliberately different from the khurpi item, whose method is mechanical.
Picking the rabi crop from a list is the seasonal classification. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because no practice is carried out.
The cultivator used for ploughing is a tillage implement in the production cycle. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, which requires constructing a model.
The statements contrast fertiliser with manure and humus, so the fertiliser judgement outcome fits. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because statements are being tested for truth, not materials sorted.
Choosing sprinkler irrigation for uneven land is the water-saving judgement, a judicious use of a resource. Kept apart from the rotating-nozzle item, which only names the method.
Winnowing by wind is a post-harvest practice. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, because a known method is recalled rather than investigated.
Broadcasting as hand-scattering of seed is a sowing method. Not C-SCI4.2-LO-1, since no design or planning creativity is required.
Classing a bacteriophage as a virus is the microorganism classification named in the outcome. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no disease is being traced.
Knowing threshing follows harvesting is knowledge of the production sequence. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1: a step order is recalled, nothing is classified.
The combine harvesting and threshing together is farm machinery in the production chain. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, which asks for a constructed model.
Gunny bags for grain storage is applied post-harvest management. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, because no resource restraint or hazard is involved.
Legumes enriching soil with nitrogen relates an effect to its cause. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which fits a fertiliser decision rather than the mechanism.
Raising soil fertility through manure or rotation is the controlled-input judgement. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1: the item asks what to do, not why it works.
Silos as bulk grain storage is applied post-harvest management. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, because nothing is built.

Neem leaves protecting stored grain is a household application, grouped with the other storage items. C-SCI4.1-LO-1 was rejected narrowly: a traditional method is named, no chemical restraint is asked for.
Naming Plasmodium as the malarial parasite ties a disease to its causative agent. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, reserved here for useful/harmful sorting.
Picking the useful microorganism from four named species is the useful/harmful classification verbatim. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, since no single disease is explained.
Fermentation as the conversion of sugar to alcohol is a process to be explained. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the chemical change rather than the organism is at issue.
Loosening and turning the soil, i.e. ploughing, is the first production practice. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, as tillage is not an input the environmental outcome restrains.
Rhizobium in root nodules is the textbook useful microorganism, so the useful/harmful classification fits. Kept apart from the legume-enrichment item, which asks for the causal effect.
Identifying sprinkler irrigation from its rotating nozzles is method recall. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, used for the uneven-land item where water saving is the point.
Separating weeds from non-weeds sorts plants by characteristics. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which covers the removal practice rather than recognising the plant.
